def _w2_qr_2level_n512(data):
    # brief-15: TWO-LEVEL DECOUPLING for the n=512 (B=640, grid-SATURATED) regime.
    # IB=16 narrow (un-spilled, 3 blocks/SM) sub-panels + ONE wide NB=32 trailing
    # per PAIR of sub-panels (trailing-pass count UNCHANGED vs the single-level
    # BLK=32 path) coupled by the cross_T T01 = -T0 (V0^T V1) T1 block. Same exact
    # geqrf (H,tau). All GEMMs tf32x3 (n=512 irreducibly tf32x3).
    #
    # Distinct from _w2_qr_2level (n>=2560): NO hybrid single-level fallback (the
    # whole point at n=512 is the IB=16 panel at every j), SATURATED-grid tiles
    # (fused on-chip wide trailing, not the grid-starved split pair), and tf32x3
    # throughout (not the 1-pass _N4096_PREC the tall-shape path uses).
    A = data.contiguous()
    B, N, _ = A.shape
    # CLONE FUSION (brief-15 iter3): the old `H = A.clone()` did a full HBM
    # read(A)+write(H) of all of A (~209us measured at n=512 B=640 -- ~4% of the
    # shape) just so the kernels could factor in place. But the FIRST outer block
    # already touches EVERY column of H: sub-panel 0 writes cols [0,IB), apply2
    # writes sub-panel 1's cols [IB,2IB), the wide trailing writes [2IB,N). So
    # block 0 reads A (src) and writes H; every later block reads+writes H in
    # place. _panel_factor2_kernel / _trailing_apply2_kernel / _trailing_fused_
    # kernel take a separate Aout dest so block 0's A-reads come from A while the
    # stores populate the uninitialized H. (Sub-panel 1 always reads H -- apply2
    # wrote its columns just before.) Saves the whole clone pass.
    H = torch.empty_like(A)
    tau = torch.zeros((B, N), device=A.device, dtype=torch.float32)

    IB = _N512_2L_IB                 # 16
    NB = _N512_2L_NB                 # 32
    IBP = 16 if IB <= 16 else 32     # padded reflector index for the cross kernels (>=IB, MMA-legal)
    Vbuf = torch.zeros((B, NB, N), device=A.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    Tbuf = torch.zeros((B, NB, NB), device=A.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    YTbuf = torch.empty((B, NB, N), device=A.device, dtype=torch.float32)

    sab, san = H.stride(0), H.stride(1)
    svb, svk, svn = Vbuf.stride(0), Vbuf.stride(1), Vbuf.stride(2)
    stb, stk, stn = Tbuf.stride(0), Tbuf.stride(1), Tbuf.stride(2)
    syb, syk, syn = YTbuf.stride(0), YTbuf.stride(1), YTbuf.stride(2)

    # split-Gram / split-YT2 partials (fill SMs on the per-matrix reductions).
    GRAM_BM = _N512_2L_GRAM_BM
    nrt_max = triton.cdiv(N, GRAM_BM)
    Gpart = torch.empty((B, nrt_max, IBP, IBP), device=A.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    sgb, sgt, sgi, sgj = Gpart.stride(0), Gpart.stride(1), Gpart.stride(2), Gpart.stride(3)
    Wpart = torch.empty((B, nrt_max, NB, NB), device=A.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    swb, swt, swk, swn = Wpart.stride(0), Wpart.stride(1), Wpart.stride(2), Wpart.stride(3)

    FBM, FBNC, FNW = _N512_2L_FBM, _N512_2L_FBNC, _N512_2L_FNW

    j = 0
    while j < N:
        pheight = N - j
        MAXH = triton.next_power_of_2(pheight)

        # CLONE FUSION: block 0's A-reads come from A; later blocks read H. The
        # store dest is always H. Sub-panel 1 is the exception -- it reads H (its
        # columns were just written by apply2), so it uses H even in block 0.
        src = A if j == 0 else H

        b0 = min(IB, N - j)
        # IB=16 sub-panel: (MAXH,16) register tile. nwp chosen so it un-spills at
        # 3 blocks/SM (gate: 167 r/thr). MAXH<=512 -> nwp=4 keeps it un-spilled.
        nwp0 = _N512_2L_PNW
        # sub-panel 0: cols [j, j+IB), V/T at offset (0,0). Reads src, writes H.
        _panel_factor2_kernel[(B,)](
            src, tau, Vbuf, Tbuf, B, N, j, pheight, b0, 0, 0,
            sab, san, svb, svk, svn, stb, stk, stn,
            H,
            BLK=IB, MAXH=MAXH, num_warps=nwp0,
        )

        b1 = min(IB, N - j - b0)
        if b1 > 0:
            # inner trailing: apply sub-panel 0's IB reflectors to ONLY sub-panel
            # 1's b1 cols. Masked NREF=IB out of the NB-wide buffer (cols IB:2IB
            # may be stale -> no per-block reset). The A_sub1 columns are read from
            # src (block 0: A); the result is written to H.
            if _N512_2L_FUSE_INNER:
                # FUSED: W kept on-chip (no YT HBM round-trip) + one launch. Each
                # program owns the full-height b1-wide strip -> race-free.
                _trailing_fused2_kernel[(triton.cdiv(b1, NB), B)](
                    src, Vbuf, Tbuf, B, N, j, pheight, b1, j + b0,
                    sab, san, svb, svk, svn, stb, stk, stn,
                    H,
                    BLK=NB, BM=_N512_2L_FI_BM, BNc=NB, NREF=IB, num_warps=_N512_2L_FI_NW,
                )
            else:
                if _N512_2L_SPLIT:
                    nrt_y2 = triton.cdiv(pheight, GRAM_BM)
                    _trailing_YT2_partW_kernel[(nrt_y2, B)](
                        src, Vbuf, Wpart, B, N, j, pheight, b1, j + b0,
                        sab, san, svb, svk, svn, swb, swt, swk, swn,
                        BLK=NB, BM=GRAM_BM, BNc=NB, NREF=IB, num_warps=4,
                    )
                    _trailing_YT2_finishW_kernel[(B,)](
                        Wpart, Tbuf, YTbuf, B, nrt_y2, b1,
                        swb, swt, swk, swn, stb, stk, stn, syb, syk, syn,
                        BLK=NB, BNc=NB, NREF=IB, num_warps=2,
                    )
                else:
                    # saturated grid: single-CTA YT2 (grid=(1,B)=640 fills the GPU).
                    _trailing_YT2_kernel[(1, B)](
                        src, Vbuf, Tbuf, YTbuf, B, N, j, pheight, b1, j + b0,
                        sab, san, svb, svk, svn, stb, stk, stn, syb, syk, syn,
                        BLK=NB, BM=_N512_2L_YT2_BM, BNc=NB, NREF=IB, num_warps=_N512_2L_YT2_NW,
                    )
                _trailing_apply2_kernel[(triton.cdiv(pheight, _N512_2L_AP2_BM), B)](
                    src, Vbuf, YTbuf, B, N, j, pheight, b1, j + b0,
                    sab, san, svb, svk, svn, syb, syk, syn,
                    H,
                    BLK=NB, BM=_N512_2L_AP2_BM, BNc=NB, NREF=IB, num_warps=_N512_2L_AP2_NW,
                )

            # sub-panel 1: cols [j+b0, j+b0+b1), V/T at offset (row IB, col IB).
            # Always reads H (apply2 just wrote these columns), writes H.
            ph1 = N - (j + b0)
            MAXH1 = triton.next_power_of_2(ph1)
            _panel_factor2_kernel[(B,)](
                H, tau, Vbuf, Tbuf, B, N, j + b0, ph1, b1, IB, IB,
                sab, san, svb, svk, svn, stb, stk, stn,
                H,
                BLK=IB, MAXH=MAXH1, num_warps=nwp0,
            )

            # cross-block T01 = -T0 (V0^T V1) T1.
            if _N512_2L_SPLIT:
                nrt_g = triton.cdiv(pheight, GRAM_BM)
                _cross_gram_kernel[(nrt_g, B)](
                    Vbuf, Gpart, B, pheight, IB,
                    svb, svk, svn, sgb, sgt, sgi, sgj,
                    BM=GRAM_BM, IBP=IBP,
                )
                _cross_finish_kernel[(B,)](
                    Gpart, Tbuf, B, nrt_g, IB,
                    sgb, sgt, sgi, sgj, stb, stk, stn,
                    IBP=IBP,
                )
            else:
                # saturated grid: single-CTA cross_T (grid=(B,)=640 fills the GPU).
                _cross_T_kernel[(B,)](
                    Vbuf, Tbuf, B, pheight, IB, IB,
                    svb, svk, svn, stb, stk, stn,
                    BM=_N512_2L_CT_BM, IBP=IBP, num_warps=_N512_2L_CT_NW,
                )

        bb = b0 + b1                      # reflectors in this outer block (<=NB)
        ncols = N - (j + bb)
        if ncols > 0:
            # ONE wide NB=32 trailing over the bulk, exact via the combined T.
            # Fused on-chip (W kept in regs, no YT HBM round-trip); race-free
            # (each program owns a full-height column strip). tf32x3 (n=512).
            # brief-22: ILP split-accumulator (NACC) + software-pipeline (NS) +
            # wide BNc=64 grafted from worker-0 brief-21 (latency-bound W-reduction).
            nct_f = triton.cdiv(ncols, FBNC)
            _trailing_fused_kernel[(nct_f, B)](
                src, Vbuf, Tbuf, B, N, j, pheight, ncols, j + bb,
                sab, san, svb, svk, svn, stb, stk, stn,
                H,
                BLK=NB, BM=FBM, BNc=FBNC, num_warps=FNW, IPREC="tf32x3",
                NACC=_N512_2L_F_NACC, NS=_N512_2L_F_NS,
            )
        j += bb

    return H, tau

Now I have complete understanding. The two-level n=512 path uses NB=32 (two IB=16 sub-panels) with a wide trailing of K=NB=32 — still thin. To make it compute-bound, I'd need NB=128/256 (8-16 sub-panels), which means the wide trailing's contraction K=128/256.

**Key strategic realization before I write code:** Let me think carefully about the FP4 economics for the wide-NB trailing, using brief-27's measured numbers.

The fundamental issue from brief-27: quantization cost. For the trailing `W=V^T A` (K=pheight contraction) and `delta=V@YT`, the data that must be quantized is V (NB×pheight) and A_trail (pheight×ncols). At n=512, pheight~512, ncols~480. Quantizing A_trail is pheight×ncols ≈ 512×480 ≈ 245K elements per matrix × B=640. That quant cost is FIXED regardless of NB. But the GEMM FLOPs = NB×ncols×pheight. So wider NB amortizes the quant-of-A cost over more FLOPs. **This is exactly the economics my brief identifies.**

But wait — there's a subtlety. In `W=V^T A`, the contraction is over pheight (the tall dimension). V is (NB, pheight), A_trail is (pheight, ncols). The output W is (NB, ncols). The contraction dimension K=pheight is ALREADY large (~512). So the W-reduction GEMM is already K-large! The problem in brief-27 was the *thin output* (NB×ncols with NB=32) and the quant overhead. Wider NB makes the output less thin AND amortizes quant.

Actually, let me reconsider. Let me re-read brief-27's exact decomposition: "pure dot_scaled W (pre-quantized)=701us vs tf32 bmm 260us (3x slower); quant_rhs(A_trail) alone=3314us (12x the whole tf32 GEMM)". So even the *pure* FP4 dot (pre-quantized) was 3x slower than tf32 bmm for W. That's because at NB=32, the W GEMM (32×480 output, K=512) is small-output — the dot_scaled MMA at NB=32 output rows is underutilized.

So widening NB to 128/256 attacks BOTH problems: (a) larger output → better dot_scaled MMA utilization, (b) more FLOPs → amortizes the fixed A-quant cost. This is genuinely the untested regime.

    #   W = V^T@A_trail (FP4) ; YT = T^T@W (tf32x3) ; A_trail = src - V@YT (FP4),

    #   "raw"   : none (factor residual fails -- diagnostic only).
    #   "corr"  : one fp32 recompute of the apply on the FP4 result (known-good,
    #             expensive PROBE).
    #   "corr1" : one tf32x3 (kernel) correction pass -- the production fast fixup.
    BLK = Vbuf.shape[1]
    KK = triton.next_power_of_2(pheight)
    BNc = _FP4_FBNC

        Vbuf.stride(0), Vbuf.stride(1), Vbuf.stride(2),

        BLK=BLK, BNc=BNc, BM=BM, KK=KK, GS=_E2M1_GROUP, GH=_E2M1_GROUP // 2,
        num_warps=_FP4_FNW,

    if mode == "raw":

    Vt = Vbuf[:, :bb, :pheight]                              # (B,bb,pheight) = V^T

I have full understanding of the FP4 infra. The brief-27 `_trailing_fused_fp4_kernel` does on-the-fly quant + dot_scaled for W and delta, with a `corr` mode that re-derives the trailing in tf32 via bmm. The fused kernel uses `KK = next_power_of_2(pheight)` and quantizes V^T and A_strip on-chip.

**Critical observation about the fused FP4 kernel:** It quantizes A_strip (the trailing columns being processed) on-the-fly per program. The quant cost is intrinsic. But importantly, this fused kernel does the W reduction with K=pheight (the FULL panel height as one MMA tile, `tl.arange(0, KK//2)`), so it does NOT chunk over rows — it loads the whole (BLK, KK) V and (BNc, KK) A. That's a HUGE register/smem footprint at pheight=512 (KK=512). This is likely why it was slow — not compute-bound efficiency but smem pressure.

Let me think about the RIGHT FP4 structure for wide-NB compute-bound. The brief explicitly says **two-level keeps panel narrow** and widen the OUTER block NB. The cleanest approach: take the existing `_w2_qr_2level_n512` (which already has the two-level structure with IB sub-panels + ONE wide trailing) and:
1. Widen NB to 128/256 (more IB=16 sub-panels per outer block).
2. Replace the wide trailing's tf32x3 GEMM with raw FP4 (one dot_scaled).
3. Add ONE re-orthogonalization/residual-correction pass to restore (H,tau) accuracy.

import torch, time

def bench(fn, iters=80, warmup=20):
    for _ in range(warmup): fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t0=time.perf_counter()
    for _ in range(iters): fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return (time.perf_counter()-t0)/iters*1e6

def e2m1_code(xs):
    a = xs.abs()
    c = torch.where(a<0.25,0, torch.where(a<0.75,1, torch.where(a<1.25,2,
        torch.where(a<1.75,3, torch.where(a<2.5,4, torch.where(a<3.5,5,
        torch.where(a<5.0,6,7))))))).to(torch.int32)
    sgn=(xs<0).to(torch.int32)
    code=(sgn<<3)|c
    return torch.where(c==0, torch.zeros_like(code), code).to(torch.uint8)

def to_blocked(s):
    # s: (M, Kb) e4m3 logical scales -> swizzled blocked layout, flattened contiguous.
    # cuBLAS wants 128-row x 4-col tiles, each stored as 32x16 (row r -> tile
    # (r//32) within the 128 block, etc). Use torchao's documented rearrange.
    M, Kb = s.shape
    Mp = ((M+127)//128)*128
    Kp = ((Kb+3)//4)*4
    sp = torch.zeros(Mp, Kp, dtype=s.dtype, device=s.device)
    sp[:M,:Kb] = s
    # reshape (Mp/128,128, Kp/4,4) -> (Mp/128, Kp/4, 32,4, 4) per the 128x4->32x16 tiling
    sp = sp.view(Mp//128, 128, Kp//4, 4)
    sp = sp.permute(0,2,1,3).contiguous()         # (Mb, Kb4, 128, 4)
    sp = sp.view(Mp//128, Kp//4, 4, 32, 4)        # split 128 = 4*32
    sp = sp.permute(0,1,3,2,4).contiguous()       # (Mb,Kb4,32,4,4)
    return sp.flatten()

    amax = xg.abs().amax(2, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-20)
    scale = (amax/6.0).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).to(torch.float32).clamp_min(1e-20)

    s = scale.squeeze(-1).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)   # (R, C//block)

    code=(sgn<<3)|c
    return torch.where(c==0, torch.zeros_like(code), code).to(torch.uint8)

def to_blocked(s):
    # s: (M, Kb) e4m3 logical scales -> swizzled blocked layout, flattened contiguous.
    # cuBLAS wants 128-row x 4-col tiles, each stored as 32x16 (row r -> tile
    # (r//32) within the 128 block, etc). Use torchao's documented rearrange.
    M, Kb = s.shape
    Mp = ((M+127)//128)*128
    Kp = ((Kb+3)//4)*4
    sp = torch.zeros(Mp, Kp, dtype=s.dtype, device=s.device)
    sp[:M,:Kb] = s
    # reshape (Mp/128,128, Kp/4,4) -> (Mp/128, Kp/4, 32,4, 4) per the 128x4->32x16 tiling
    sp = sp.view(Mp//128, 128, Kp//4, 4)
    sp = sp.permute(0,2,1,3).contiguous()         # (Mb, Kb4, 128, 4)
    sp = sp.view(Mp//128, Kp//4, 4, 32, 4)        # split 128 = 4*32
    sp = sp.permute(0,1,3,2,4).contiguous()       # (Mb,Kb4,32,4,4)
    return sp.flatten()

import torch, time, triton
import triton.language as tl
dev="cuda"
torch.manual_seed(0)

def bench(fn, iters=60, warmup=20):
    for _ in range(warmup): fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t0=time.perf_counter()
    for _ in range(iters): fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return (time.perf_counter()-t0)/iters*1e6

# ---- Fused Triton NVFP4 quant: x[R,C] -> packed (R,C//2) f4x2 + e4m3 scale in
#      cuBLAS-SWIZZLED layout, in one kernel. block=16.
@triton.jit
def _e2m1_code(xs):
    a=tl.abs(xs)
    c=tl.where(a<0.25,0,tl.where(a<0.75,1,tl.where(a<1.25,2,tl.where(a<1.75,3,
      tl.where(a<2.5,4,tl.where(a<3.5,5,tl.where(a<5.0,6,7)))))))
    sgn=(xs<0).to(tl.int32)
    code=((sgn<<3)|c).to(tl.int32)
    return tl.where(c==0, tl.zeros_like(code), code)

@triton.jit
def _quant_nvfp4_kernel(X, P, S, R, C, sx0, sx1, sp0, sp1, Sb_M, Sb_K,
                        BM: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr, NBLK: tl.constexpr):
    # X[R,C] fp32 -> P[R,C//2] uint8 packed e2m1 + S swizzled e4m3 scales.
    # NBLK = C//BLOCK groups along C. Swizzle: scale for (row r, group g) goes to
    # flat index per cuBLAS 128x4 tiling. One program = BM rows.
    pid=tl.program_id(0)

def check_implementation(data: input_t, output: output_t) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    a = data
    batch, n, _ = a.shape
    factor_rtol = _property_rtol(n, _FACTOR_RTOL_FACTOR)
    orth_rtol = _property_rtol(n, _ORTH_RTOL_FACTOR)

    if not isinstance(output, tuple) or len(output) != 2:
        return False, "output must be a tuple `(H, tau)`"

    h, tau = output
    error = _check_tensor("H", h, (batch, n, n), a.device)
    if error is not None:
        return False, error
    error = _check_tensor("tau", tau, (batch, n), a.device)
    if error is not None:
        return False, error

    q = torch.linalg.householder_product(h, tau)
    r = torch.triu(h)
    if not torch.isfinite(q).all().item():
        return False, "Q materialized from `(H, tau)` contains NaN or Inf"
    if not torch.isfinite(r).all().item():
        return False, "R extracted from `triu(H)` contains NaN or Inf"

    a_check = a.double()
    q_check = q.double()
    r_check = r.double()
    projected = q_check.transpose(-1, -2) @ a_check
    if not torch.isfinite(projected).all().item():
        return False, "Q.T @ A contains NaN or Inf"

    factor_residual = _matrix_l1_norm(r_check - projected)
    factor_scale = _matrix_l1_norm(a_check)
    factor_allowed = factor_rtol * factor_scale
    factor_scaled = _scaled_residual(factor_residual, factor_scale, n)
    if not torch.isfinite(factor_scaled).all().item():
        return False, "R - Q.T @ A residual produced NaN or Inf"
    factor_failed = factor_residual > factor_allowed
    if bool(factor_failed.any().item()):
        worst = int(factor_scaled.argmax().item())
        return False, (
            "R - Q.T @ A is too large: "
            f"matrix={worst}, residual={factor_residual[worst].item():.3g}, "
            f"allowed={factor_allowed[worst].item():.3g}, "
            f"scaled={factor_scaled[worst].item():.3g}"
        )

    eye = torch.eye(n, device=a.device, dtype=torch.float64).expand(batch, n, n)
    qtq = q_check.transpose(-1, -2) @ q_check
    if not torch.isfinite(qtq).all().item():
        return False, "Q.T @ Q contains NaN or Inf"
    orth_residual = _matrix_l1_norm(qtq - eye).amax()
    orth_scale = _matrix_l1_norm(eye).amax()
    orth_allowed = orth_rtol * orth_scale
    orth_scaled = _scaled_residual(orth_residual, orth_scale, n)
    if not torch.isfinite(orth_scaled).all().item():
        return False, "Q.T @ Q residual produced NaN or Inf"
    if orth_residual.item() > orth_allowed.item():
        return False, (
            "Q is not orthogonal enough: "
            f"residual={orth_residual.item():.3g}, allowed={orth_allowed.item():.3g}, "
            f"scaled={orth_scaled.item():.3g}"
        )

    lower = torch.tril(projected, diagonal=-1)
    tri_residual = _matrix_l1_norm(lower).amax()
    tri_scale = _matrix_l1_norm(a_check).amax()
    tri_scaled = _scaled_residual(tri_residual, tri_scale, n)

    recon = q_check @ r_check
    if not torch.isfinite(recon).all().item():
        return False, "Q @ R contains NaN or Inf"
    recon_residual = _matrix_l1_norm(recon - a_check).amax()
    recon_scale = _matrix_l1_norm(a_check).amax()
    recon_scaled = _scaled_residual(recon_residual, recon_scale, n)

    return True, (
        f"factor_rtol={factor_rtol:.3g}; "
        f"orth_rtol={orth_rtol:.3g}; "
        f"scaled_factor_residual={factor_scaled.amax().item():.3g}; "
        f"scaled_reconstruction_residual={recon_scaled.item():.3g}; "
        f"scaled_triangular_residual={tri_scaled.item():.3g}; "
        f"scaled_orthogonality_residual={orth_scaled.item():.3g}; "
        f"batch={batch}; n={n}"
    )

# WHY THIS BLOCK EXISTS. brief-23 and brief-27 both concluded "FP4 dead" but
# tested the WRONG mechanism (error-corrected fp4x3 = too many MMAs; or the
# SLOW Triton tl.dot_scaled path on the thin trailing). brief-35 re-tested RAW
# NVFP4 via the CORRECT fast backend -- cuBLAS torch._scaled_mm with packed
# float4_e2m1fn_x2 data + e4m3 block scales in the swizzled layout -- across
# EVERY shape (n=512/1024/2048/4096) and EVERY block width (NB=32..256), both
# the W=V^T@A and delta=V@YT trailing GEMMs. The banked helpers below are that
# CORRECT fast path (they CORRECT brief-27's slow Triton dot_scaled infra).
#
# THE MEASURED VERDICT (idle-B200, autocuda exclusive):
#  (1) cuBLAS NVFP4 *dot-only* (pre-packed) GENUINELY BEATS bf16/tf32 -- so
#      NVFP4 is NOT slow: 0.55x @512^3, 0.67x @1024^3, 0.61x @2048^3, 0.26x
#      @4096^3 (3.9x). The MMA win is REAL and biggest for large compute-bound
#      SQUARE GEMMs. This is the leader's lever.
#  (2) BUT QR's Householder trailing has NO compute-bound GEMM: it is rank-NB
#      (THIN) -- W=V^T@A and delta=V@YT have a small (NB-sized) output. The FLOPs
#      (NB*pheight*ncols) are tiny vs the operand BYTES that must be quantized
#      (pheight*ncols, INDEPENDENT of NB). Quantization is a fixed cost-per-byte
#      a thin GEMM can never amortize. So WIDENING NB does NOT help (the brief's
#      central hypothesis): the A-quant floor is unchanged while only the MMA
#      (already a small fraction) grows. Measured W=V^T@A @n=512: FP4(quant+dot)
#      is 18-20x SLOWER than tf32 bmm at EVERY NB 32..256; quant of A ALONE is
#      8-15x the whole tf32 GEMM. delta=V@YT: 2.9x..11.7x slower, WORSE with
#      wider NB. Large-N is no better: n=4096 B=2 W is 8-25x slower (quant of
#      the 4096-tall operands ~2490us dominates regardless of NB); n=2048 B=8
#      46-121x. Even a FUSED Triton quant kernel feeding cuBLAS (kills 10x of
#      the Python-quant cost) is still 3.4-12x slower than bf16 single-matrix
#      (quant > GEMM-savings at n<=2048).
#  (3) The BATCHED dominant shapes (n=512 B=640, n=1024 B=60) are DOUBLY walled:
#      cuBLAS _scaled_mm is per-matrix -> a B=640 loop is 54.7x slower than one
#      bf16 bmm (pure launch overhead, even pre-packed); and torch 2.11's
#      _scaled_grouped_mm does NOT support FP4 (FP8/MXFP8 e8m0 only -- it errors
#      "For FP8 ... or MXFP8 ..."), so there is no one-launch batched FP4 path.
#  (4) The output CONTRACT forces Householder (H,tau): check_implementation does
#      Q=householder_product(H,tau), R=triu(H). CholeskyQR's explicit Q cannot be
#      expressed as packed reflectors without a full O(mn^2) Householder pass --
#      so the one formulation with a compute-bound GEMM (Gram G=A^T A) cannot
#      yield the required (H,tau) cheaply. (Confirms the audit's CholeskyQR kill.)
# NET: NVFP4 wins for compute-bound square GEMMs but CANNOT accelerate this
# problem's batched THIN Householder trailing in ANY regime/width reachable from
# PyTorch/Triton. The accuracy seam (raw FP4 orthogonality passes; one tf32
# apply-correction fixes the factor residual) is real and was re-confirmed, but
# it is moot without a throughput win. The leader's NVFP4 advantage must come
# from a formulation/precision-routing this Householder family does not share.
#
# The helpers are kept (default-OFF, unreferenced) so a future brief can reuse
# the CORRECT fast cuBLAS path (swizzle + fused quant) instead of re-deriving it.
# =============================================================================
_NVFP4_CUBLAS = int(_os.environ.get("QR_NVFP4_CUBLAS", "0"))   # 0 = OFF (parent)


@triton.jit
def _nvfp4_quant_kernel(
    X, P, S, R, C,
    sx0, sx1, sp0, sp1, Sb_K,
    BM: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr, NBLK: tl.constexpr,
):
    # X[R,C] fp32 -> P[R,C//2] uint8 (packed e2m1, two per byte) + S e4m3 block
    # scales in the cuBLAS SWIZZLED layout (128-row x 4-col tiles -> 32x16),
    # block=BLOCK (16 for NVFP4). One program = BM rows. This is the FAST path
    # (one fused kernel) that cuBLAS torch._scaled_mm consumes directly.
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    rm = pid * BM + tl.arange(0, BM)
    rmask = rm < R
    half = tl.arange(0, BLOCK // 2)
    for g in range(0, NBLK):
        base = g * BLOCK
        ce = base + 2 * half
        co = base + 2 * half + 1
        xe = tl.load(X + rm[:, None] * sx0 + ce[None, :] * sx1, mask=rmask[:, None], other=0.0)
        xo = tl.load(X + rm[:, None] * sx0 + co[None, :] * sx1, mask=rmask[:, None], other=0.0)
        amax = tl.maximum(tl.max(tl.abs(xe), 1), tl.max(tl.abs(xo), 1))
        amax = tl.where(amax < 1e-20, 1e-20, amax)
        scale = (amax / 6.0)
        sc = scale[:, None]
        ne = _e2m1_code(xe / sc)
        no = _e2m1_code(xo / sc)
        packed = (ne | (no << 4)).to(tl.uint8)
        pcols = g * (BLOCK // 2) + half
        tl.store(P + rm[:, None] * sp0 + pcols[None, :] * sp1, packed, mask=rmask[:, None])
        # swizzled e4m3 scale store: flat index per cuBLAS 128x4 -> 32x16 tiling.
        sc8 = scale.to(tl.float8e4nv)
        r = rm
        outer = (r // 128) * Sb_K + (g // 4)
        inner = (r % 32) * 16 + ((r % 128) // 32) * 4 + (g % 4)
        flat = outer * 512 + inner
        tl.store(S + flat, sc8, mask=rmask)


def _nvfp4_quant(x, block=16):
    # x[R,C] fp32 (C a multiple of block) -> (packed float4_e2m1fn_x2 [R,C//2],
    # swizzled e4m3 scale flat tensor) ready for torch._scaled_mm.
    R, C = x.shape
    P = torch.empty(R, C // 2, device=x.device, dtype=torch.uint8)
    NBLK = C // block
    Mp = ((R + 127) // 128) * 128
    Kp = ((NBLK + 3) // 4) * 4
    S = torch.zeros(Mp * Kp, device=x.device, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    BM = 128
    _nvfp4_quant_kernel[(triton.cdiv(R, BM),)](
        x, P, S, R, C, x.stride(0), x.stride(1), P.stride(0), P.stride(1),
        Kp // 4, BM=BM, BLOCK=block, NBLK=NBLK,
    )
    return P.view(torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2), S


def _nvfp4_mm(a, b, block=16):
    # a[M,K] @ b[K,N] (fp32) -> bf16 [M,N] via cuBLAS NVFP4. Single matrix only:
    # batched is per-matrix-launch-bound (54.7x at B=640) and grouped FP4 is
    # unsupported -- see the falsification header. Kept for reuse, not hot-path.
    M, K = a.shape
    ap, asc = _nvfp4_quant(a, block)
    bp, bsc = _nvfp4_quant(b.t().contiguous(), block)
    return torch._scaled_mm(ap, bp.t(), scale_a=asc, scale_b=bsc, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16)

@triton.jit
def _nvfp4_quant_kernel(
    X, P, S, R, C,
    sx0, sx1, sp0, sp1, Sb_K,
    BM: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr, NBLK: tl.constexpr,
):
    # X[R,C] fp32 -> P[R,C//2] uint8 (packed e2m1, two per byte) + S e4m3 block
    # scales in the cuBLAS SWIZZLED layout (128-row x 4-col tiles -> 32x16),
    # block=BLOCK (16 for NVFP4). One program = BM rows. This is the FAST path
    # (one fused kernel) that cuBLAS torch._scaled_mm consumes directly.
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    rm = pid * BM + tl.arange(0, BM)
    rmask = rm < R
    half = tl.arange(0, BLOCK // 2)
    for g in range(0, NBLK):
        base = g * BLOCK
        ce = base + 2 * half
        co = base + 2 * half + 1
        xe = tl.load(X + rm[:, None] * sx0 + ce[None, :] * sx1, mask=rmask[:, None], other=0.0)
        xo = tl.load(X + rm[:, None] * sx0 + co[None, :] * sx1, mask=rmask[:, None], other=0.0)
        amax = tl.maximum(tl.max(tl.abs(xe), 1), tl.max(tl.abs(xo), 1))
        amax = tl.where(amax < 1e-20, 1e-20, amax)
        scale = (amax / 6.0)
        sc = scale[:, None]
        ne = _e2m1_code(xe / sc)
        no = _e2m1_code(xo / sc)
        packed = (ne | (no << 4)).to(tl.uint8)
        pcols = g * (BLOCK // 2) + half
        tl.store(P + rm[:, None] * sp0 + pcols[None, :] * sp1, packed, mask=rmask[:, None])
        # swizzled e4m3 scale store: flat index per cuBLAS 128x4 -> 32x16 tiling.
        sc8 = scale.to(tl.float8e4nv)
        r = rm
        outer = (r // 128) * Sb_K + (g // 4)
        inner = (r % 32) * 16 + ((r % 128) // 32) * 4 + (g % 4)
        flat = outer * 512 + inner
        tl.store(S + flat, sc8, mask=rmask)


def _nvfp4_quant(x, block=16):
    # x[R,C] fp32 (C a multiple of block) -> (packed float4_e2m1fn_x2 [R,C//2],
    # swizzled e4m3 scale flat tensor) ready for torch._scaled_mm.
    R, C = x.shape
    P = torch.empty(R, C // 2, device=x.device, dtype=torch.uint8)
    NBLK = C // block
    Mp = ((R + 127) // 128) * 128
    Kp = ((NBLK + 3) // 4) * 4
    S = torch.zeros(Mp * Kp, device=x.device, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    BM = 128
    _nvfp4_quant_kernel[(triton.cdiv(R, BM),)](
        x, P, S, R, C, x.stride(0), x.stride(1), P.stride(0), P.stride(1),
        Kp // 4, BM=BM, BLOCK=block, NBLK=NBLK,
    )
    return P.view(torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2), S


def _nvfp4_mm(a, b, block=16):
    # a[M,K] @ b[K,N] (fp32) -> bf16 [M,N] via cuBLAS NVFP4. Single matrix only:
    # batched is per-matrix-launch-bound (54.7x at B=640) and grouped FP4 is
    # unsupported -- see the falsification header. Kept for reuse, not hot-path.
    M, K = a.shape
    ap, asc = _nvfp4_quant(a, block)
    bp, bsc = _nvfp4_quant(b.t().contiguous(), block)
    return torch._scaled_mm(ap, bp.t(), scale_a=asc, scale_b=bsc, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16)

Iteration logged. Now, before concluding, let me reconsider whether I've truly exhausted the brief. The brief is HIGH PRIORITY and emphatic about not concluding FP4 is dead. I've rigorously falsified the trailing-GEMM approach. But let me reconsider ONE angle I haven't fully tested that could genuinely flip the economics and is faithful to "find WHICH compute-bound formulation makes raw-FP4 net-win":

**The PANEL's reflector computation involves a Gram-like reduction (V^T V) for the compact-WY T and cross-T.** For the large-N shapes (n=4096), the panel does the dominant work. But the panel reflectors require sequential dependency — not a single GEMM.

The truly unexplored compute-bound formulation: **what if I batch ALL the small per-matrix GEMMs into ONE giant GEMM by exploiting block-diagonal structure?** No — block-diagonal GEMMs waste FLOPs.

Let me reconsider the dot-only numbers once more. The KEY finding is cuBLAS NVFP4 dot-only beats bf16 even at 512³ (0.55x). The ONLY thing killing it is quantization. **What if the quantization could be amortized by reusing quantized operands across the right-looking sweep?**

In right-looking blocked QR, outer block j's trailing reads A[:, j+NB:] (the trailing). Block j+1's panel reads A[:, j+NB:j+2NB] (a slice of what j just wrote). The data is WRITTEN by j's trailing and READ by j+1. If j's trailing wrote A in FP4 form... but then the panel needs full precision to factor.

There's genuinely no reuse: each element of A is read ~once per outer block it's trailing for, and it's MODIFIED each time. The quantization can't be cached because the values change.

I'm confident the falsification is complete and correct. The brief's hypothesis is thoroughly tested and falsified with measured data, and I've corrected the operator's premise: NVFP4's MMA IS fast (so it's not "FP4 dead"), but QR's structure (thin trailing + batched-small + Householder-output-contract) blocks every path to exploiting it.

Everything is consistent: branch `worker-2-brief-35` at clean HEAD `412298c7`, working tree clean, brief_start/iteration/brief_stop all logged. Brief-35 is fully explored and I've returned to the manager.

## Summary for the manager

**Brief-35 (NVFP4, operator-confirmed #1 path) — EXHAUSTED → comprehensive measured falsification, operator's premise corrected.**

**Outcome:** Best stays parent `8b1b634e` = **2544µs** (matches the 2547µs threshold). HEAD `412298c7` is a **purely-additive** (138 insertions / 0 deletions) default-OFF infra commit; `custom_kernel` is byte-identical to the accepted parent, so remote behavior is unchanged. Validate PASS (all 22 incl ill-conditioned + invariance guard CLEAN), no "stream" substring. **Not submitted** (parent-equivalent, no beat).

**The key correction to the operator's premise.** Re-testing RAW NVFP4 via the *correct* fast backend — cuBLAS `torch._scaled_mm` with packed `float4_e2m1fn_x2` + e4m3 swizzled block scales, not brief-27's slow Triton `tl.dot_scaled` — shows the NVFP4 **MMA genuinely beats bf16** (dot-only: 0.55x@512³, 0.67x@1024³, 0.61x@2048³, **0.26x@4096³**). So NVFP4 is *not* slow; the prior "FP4 dead" conclusions blamed the wrong thing.

**Why the wide-NB hypothesis is nonetheless falsified (measured, idle-B200).** QR's Householder trailing is rank-NB (thin): its FLOPs (NB·pheight·ncols) are tiny vs the operand bytes that must be quantized (pheight·ncols, **independent of NB**). Quantization is a fixed cost-per-byte a thin GEMM can never amortize, and widening NB does *not* lower the A-quant floor. W=V^T@A @n=512 is **18–20× slower** than tf32 bmm at every NB 32→256; delta=V@YT 2.9–11.7× (worse wider); n=4096 8–25×; n=2048 46–121×. Dominant batched shapes are doubly walled: per-matrix `_scaled_mm` loop is 54.7× slower (B=640 launches) and `_scaled_grouped_mm` has **no FP4 support** (FP8/MXFP8 only). The output contract (`householder_product(H,tau)`) independently blocks the one compute-bound formulation (CholeskyQR Gram).

**Banked for the fleet (default-OFF, zero build/runtime cost):** `_nvfp4_quant_kernel` (fused Triton fp32→packed-e2m1 + e4m3 in the cuBLAS swizzled 128×4→32×16 layout, one launch), `_nvfp4_quant`, `_nvfp4_mm`, `_e2m1_code` — the correct fast cuBLAS path + swizzle that brief-27 lacked.

**Recommendation:** treat NVFP4-on-trailing as closed; the #1 (`submission_nvfp4.py @1360µs`) edge is almost certainly structural — note `s14.py @1418µs` (non-FP4) is only 4% behind the FP4 leader, so the algorithm, not FP4, is most of our 21% gap.
